newsitem.title: USA: Chevron Information to cut 600 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Information to cut 600 jobs.

text.p: Chevron Information Technology Co Monday named Dave Clementz president and said it plans to eliminate a total of 600 jobs over the next two years as part of a restructuring effort.
In a statement, Chevron Information Clementz appointment is effective Feb. 15.
As a result of the company's restructuring the company said it expects to see a $50 million annual reduction in costs once all facets of the redirection are in place.
Chevron Information currently has about 1,660 employees.
The company said 200 employees from other Chevron companies providing similar services will be moved into the new organization, consolidating personnel and equipment.
Approximately 100 positions will be eliminated in the first phase of the plan, which is expected to be completed by April 1.

During 1998, approximately 500 additional positions will be eliminated as operations are streamlined, outsourced or discontinued. By the end of 1998, Chevron Information said it expects to have about 1,200 employees.
Clementz, 51, currently serves as president of Chevron Petroleum Technology Co. He replaces Bill Houghton, who is retiring.
